title: Zaynab's voice
hook: Husayn's sister Zaynab speaks with courage before Yazid in Damascus

segments.voice: Yesterday: Ashura, a day of rescue that also became a day of grief at Karbala. Your line was the tenth day.

A captive is not expected to speak. She is expected to walk where she is led and to keep her eyes down. This captive had just lost her brothers, her sons and her nephews, and she was being marched from Iraq to Syria. She was Zaynab, daughter of Ali and Fatima, granddaughter of the Prophet, peace be upon him. And when she was brought before the men who held her, she did not stay silent.
screen: `A CAPTIVE ON THE ROAD.` → `BROUGHT BEFORE HER CAPTORS.` → `SHE DID NOT STAY SILENT.`

segments.voice: The first time is in Kufa, before the governor, Ibn Ziyad. The histories say he ordered Husayn's sick son, Ali, to be killed, and Zaynab threw her arms around her nephew: if you kill him, kill me with him. The governor let the boy live. Shia accounts add an exchange repeated to this day. The governor mocks her: how do you see what God has done to your brother? She answers: I saw nothing but beauty. Those who tell it hear in her answer that the fallen had chosen their path, and God had honored them. Then Damascus, and the court of Yazid. Al-Tabari tells of a man in the court who asked Yazid to give him one of the captive girls, and the girl clung to Zaynab in terror. Zaynab told him to his face that he had no right to her, and neither did his master. Yazid, angry, said he could do it if he wished. She answered that he could not, unless he left the religion. The girl was not handed over. A collection of speeches by the writer Ibn Tayfur records a sermon she gave in that court, quoting the Qur'an back at the man on the throne: that evil is the end of those who do evil. Shia Muslims honor Zaynab as the voice of Karbala, who carried its story out of captivity so it could not be buried. Sunni Muslims honor her as the Prophet's granddaughter, a woman of patience and strength. Her courage has a particular shape. She did not raise an army. She held a boy, shielded a girl, and spoke.
screen: `IF YOU KILL HIM, KILL ME WITH HIM.` · `I SAW NOTHING BUT BEAUTY.` · `NO RIGHT TO HER.` · `A SERMON IN THE COURT.` · then, large: `ZAYNAB SPOKE.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind one person with power over you, or over someone near you: a boss, a landlord, a relative everyone tiptoes around. Find one true thing that needs saying, then the gentlest way to say it without losing the truth. Zaynab's answers in court were short, so fit yours into one sentence, and simply hold it.
Zaynab's voice. Husayn's sister, a captive, who shielded her nephew in Kufa and spoke before Yazid in Damascus, so the story of Karbala was told. Today's word.
Your line: Zaynab spoke. Grief and captivity did not silence her. Day eight hundred ninety-two, done.

howItsDone: Shia Muslims retell Zaynab's words in Kufa and Damascus in Muharram gatherings, and her shrine near Damascus is a place of pilgrimage; Sunni Muslims honor her as the Prophet's granddaughter.

chat.says: What did Zaynab do after Karbala?
options: As a captive, she shielded her nephew and spoke before Yazid.
She gathered a new army in Medina to fight Yazid.
She stayed silent, keeping her eyes down all the way.
chat.meaning: In Kufa she held her nephew Ali and he was spared; in Damascus she shielded a captive girl and spoke in Yazid's court. She did not raise an army.
